summary: The @ input diverges in the SELF-key branch of getpos.c:getpos(). C resets every location-cycle index, restores the cursor to u.ux/u.uy, then reaches nxtc without changing the message or ending targeting. JavaScript has no getpos.self branch and treats @ as an unknown direction, so namefloorobj continues from the wrong selected coordinate.

source.branch: When c equals gc.Cmd.spkeys[NHKF_GETPOS_SELF] (default @), getpos() resets every gidx entry, assigns cx/cy from u.ux/u.uy, and jumps to nxtc. That path updates gg.getposx/getposy, map cursor and screen, then reads the next key.
callers: do_name.c:namefloorobj() calls getpos(&cc, FALSE, buf) before resolving the selected floor object; js/do_name.js:namefloorobj() calls js/getpos.js:getpos() on the same path.
dependencies: B delivery 801cda8f8eab1e9f801f8b4dbf21baf7e745fcf9 already supplies the separate getpos.menu toggle branch and is an ancestor of this task base.
The existing local gidx array stores the source location-cycle indices; the SELF branch resets it without changing message state.

evidence: The saved admitted v48 evaluation at challenges/evaluations/accepted-1cefd15ca83512eb920105c96202699a1b04a8e0-v48.json reports this case at 59/60 screens, 2587/2587 RNG calls, and 60/60 cursors; its first mismatch is segment 0 step 50 on @, screen row 0 column 0 (C h, JS C). The recording is challenges/cases/v48/v48-name-floor-object-attempt5.session.json.

nethack-c/upstream/src/getpos.c:getpos() lines 997-1004 implement NHKF_GETPOS_SELF: zero all gidx entries, set cx=u.ux and cy=u.uy, then goto nxtc. The shared nxtc path updates gg.getposx/getposy, calls curs(WIN_MAP,cx,cy), and flushes the screen. It emits no message and does not leave the targeting loop.

The production caller is nethack-c/upstream/src/do_name.c:namefloorobj() lines 679-771, which initializes cc to the hero and calls getpos(&cc,FALSE,buf). js/do_name.js:namefloorobj() already wires that route into js/getpos.js:getpos(). At the mismatch, the recipe has selected an offset cursor before @; the missing JS special-key arm instead falls through to the non-force unknown-direction exit path.

The omitted SELF branch proves the previous whole-getpos completion evidence was partial. The follow-up covers getpos.c:getpos 771–1167 and its return-valued getpos_menu dependency 665–725, including queued input, mouse selection, movement prefixes, filtering, message state and exits.
